hook: *4* Hyderabad eateries lose food licences after raids
hook_b: *4* Hyderabad eateries lose food licences after raids
tldr: TG SAFE suspended FSSAI licences of Alpha Hotel (Secunderabad), Laham House (Jubilee Hills), Pandem Kodi (Vengal Rao Nagar) and Spice Kitchen (Gowlidoddy) after Nov 18 inspections found cockroaches, houseflies, clogged drains and unlabelled food.

beats.what: Five enforcement teams inspected 10 eateries on Nov 18 after consumer complaints; four licences were suspended.
beats.why: Inspectors reported cockroach infestation, rusted knives, and veg and non-veg food stored together.
beats.care: The four must stop operating; show-cause notices go to outlets in Nizampet, Banjara Hills and Serilingampally.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: The Hindu (Nov 18): New Blue Star Restaurant, Kukatpally, and Srinivasa Boys Hostel, Panjagutta, were closed for operating without licences.

cards.q: Do raids like this change where you eat out?

qs: Should inspection results be shown at restaurant entrances?

facts.t: TG SAFE collected *8* food samples on suspicion of adulteration during Wednesday's raids.

viz.verdict: Six of 10 places shut or suspended

watch: Re-inspections and whether suspended outlets get licences back after fixing lapses.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: FSSAI licences of four restaurants in Hyderabad suspended over food safety violations

fact: Food safety raids shut *four* Hyderabad eateries, including Jubilee Hills' Laham House
twist: Two more places, in Kukatpally and Panjagutta, were found running with no FSSAI licence at all.
